title: Write Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
student_objective: I can write two-variable linear inequalities from graphs, tables, and real situations and explain the boundary and shading.

concept_cards.title: Boundary first
concept_cards.content: Replace the inequality sign with = to draw the boundary line. The boundary separates the coordinate plane into two possible solution regions.

concept_cards.title: Solid or dashed?
concept_cards.content: Use a solid boundary for ≤ or ≥ because equality is included. Use a dashed boundary for < or > because equality is not included.

concept_cards.title: Shade the solution side
concept_cards.content: Use a test point such as (0,0) when it is not on the boundary. If the point makes the inequality true, shade the side containing it.

concept_cards.title: Write from a graph or context
concept_cards.content: Read the boundary line, decide inclusion from solid/dashed style, then use the shaded side or words such as at most and at least to choose the inequality symbol.

boundary_style.teacher_signal: Student confuses solid and dashed boundaries.

write_inequality.teacher_signal: Student has the correct line but wrong inequality direction or inclusion.

items.prompt: For y>2x-1, should the boundary line be solid or dashed?
items.tutor_behavior: The strict sign > does not include boundary points.

items.prompt: Does the point (0,0) satisfy y≤x+3? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Substitute x=0 and y=0 into the inequality.
hint_steps: Substitute the point into both sides.

solution_steps.explanation: The point lies in the solution region.

items.prompt: A graph has boundary y=2x-1 drawn dashed and the region above the line is shaded. Write the inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: Above means y is greater than the line; dashed means equality is excluded.
hint_steps: Above the line means y is greater.

items.prompt: A graph has boundary y=-x+4 drawn solid and the region below the line is shaded. Write the inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: Below means y is less than the line; solid means equality is included.
hint_steps: Below means y is less than the boundary value.

solution_steps.explanation: Shade below and include the boundary.

items.prompt: Adult tickets x cost $12 and student tickets y cost $8. The event can collect at most $120. Write an inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: At most means the total cannot exceed 120.

items.prompt: A graph has solid boundary y=3x-2 and shading above the line. Write the inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: Above means greater; solid includes equality.
hint_steps: Above means y is greater than the boundary.

items.prompt: For y<-2x+5, state the boundary style and shading direction as dashed, below or solid, above.
items.tutor_behavior: The sign < is strict and means y-values below the line.
hint_steps: y is less than the boundary output.

items.prompt: Items x cost $4 and items y cost $6. The budget is no more than $60. Write the inequality.
A graph has dashed boundary y=x+2 and shading below. Write the inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: Dashed excludes equality and below means less than.

items.prompt: A graph has solid boundary y=-3x+1 and shading above. Write the inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: Solid includes the line; above means greater.

solution_steps.explanation: Use greater-than-or-equal because the boundary is solid.

items.prompt: A club needs at least 40 volunteer hours. Adults x contribute 3 hours each and students y contribute 2 hours each. Write the inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: At least means the total must be 40 or greater.

items.prompt: Dashed boundary y=4x-3 with shading above. Write the inequality.
Solid boundary y=-2x+7 with shading below. Write the inequality.
Does (2,1) satisfy y≥x-2? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Test the point in the inequality.
hint_steps: The statement is true, so yes.

solution_steps.explanation: It lies in the solution set.

items.prompt: For y<5, is the boundary horizontal or vertical, and is it solid or dashed? Answer horizontal, dashed.
items.tutor_behavior: y=5 is horizontal and < is strict.

items.prompt: A fundraiser earns $10 from each x-item and $15 from each y-item and needs at least $150. Write the inequality.
